notes: API names are matched against the declaration Clang resolved for each call: 'Class::method' matches when Class is the declaring class, the object's static type or one of its base classes; a bare name matches a free function. Detection logic lives in backend/security_engine/*_detector.py.

rules.description: Network communication functionality detected.
rules.detection_condition: A function calls a network API (client connect/read/write, HTTP request, UDP packet, MQTT, sockets). One finding per function. INFO in project code and in dependencies whose stated purpose involves networking; LOW in dependencies whose purpose is unknown.
required_context: dependency purpose from registry or library manifest
rules.explanation: Networking is normal for IoT firmware. The finding documents where communication happens so it can be reviewed; it is not evidence of misuse.
rules.recommendation: Verify that this code needs the detected network communication.
limitations: Calls through function pointers or callbacks are not resolved.
Network APIs not listed in this rule are not recognised.

rules.description: Dependency performs network communication that its stated purpose does not explain.
rules.detection_condition: NET001 conditions hold in dependency code, and the package's registry description/keywords or library manifest is available and contains no networking term (wifi, network, http, mqtt, web, cloud, iot, ...).
required_context: dependency purpose from registry metadata or library.properties/library.json
rules.explanation: A sensor or display driver that opens network connections sends or receives data the application author may not expect.
rules.recommendation: Review this dependency's network code and confirm why it communicates, or replace the dependency.
limitations: Purpose matching uses keywords and can miss networking features described in other words.

rules.description: Hard-coded remote endpoint passed to a network call.
rules.detection_condition: A network call receives a constant host name, IP address or URL. INFO in project code (endpoint inventory), MEDIUM in dependency code.
rules.explanation: The destination is fixed in the firmware. In application code this is usually intentional; in a library it means the library decides where data goes.
rules.recommendation: Confirm that the endpoint is expected and owned by you or a trusted service.
limitations: Endpoints built at run time (string concatenation, configuration) are not resolved.

rules.description: Unencrypted protocol URL used for network communication.
rules.detection_condition: A constant http://, ws:// or mqtt:// URL is passed to a network call.
rules.explanation: Data sent over plain HTTP/WS/MQTT can be read and modified by anyone on the path.
rules.recommendation: Use https://, wss:// or mqtts:// with certificate verification.
limitations: Plain TCP connections without a URL scheme are not classified.

rules.description: TLS certificate verification disabled.
rules.detection_condition: setInsecure() is called on a WiFiClientSecure/NetworkClientSecure object.
rules.explanation: Without certificate verification the device accepts any server, so the connection is open to interception.
rules.recommendation: Load the server's CA certificate with setCACert() instead of setInsecure().

rules.description: Potential hardcoded credential detected in source code.
rules.detection_condition: A string literal that is not empty or a placeholder is (a) assigned to a variable or macro whose name indicates a secret (password, pass, pwd, secret, token, api_key, auth, psk, private_key), or (b) passed in a credential position of a known API (WiFi.begin password, WiFi.softAP password, MQTT connect user/password, HTTPClient::setAuthorization, ArduinoOTA.setPassword, WebServer::authenticate, setPreSharedKey).
required_context: identifier name or API argument position
rules.explanation: Secrets in source code end up in version control and in the firmware image, where they can be extracted from the flash.
rules.recommendation: Provision secrets at run time (NVS/Preferences, provisioning, secure storage) and rotate any secret that was committed.
limitations: Secrets with non-descriptive names passed through unknown APIs are not recognised.
Values are redacted in the report; only the first two characters and the length are shown.

rules.description: String literal matches a known secret or private-key format.
rules.detection_condition: A string literal matches one of the documented token formats (AWS access key id, GitHub token, Slack token, Stripe key, Google API key, JWT, PEM private key).
rules.explanation: These formats are issued by services as credentials; a literal in this format is very likely a real or test secret.
rules.recommendation: Remove the secret from source code and revoke it at the issuing service.
limitations: Only the listed formats are recognised.

rules.description: Credential written to log output.
rules.detection_condition: A logging call (Serial/Print print, println, printf, log_*, esp_log_write, printf) receives a variable or macro whose name indicates a secret, or a value already identified as a hardcoded credential.
required_context: credential-like identifier or known credential value
rules.explanation: Serial and log output is readable by anyone with physical access or log collection; secrets printed there are disclosed.
rules.recommendation: Never print secrets; log a masked value or a success/failure flag instead.
limitations: Secrets copied into other variables before printing are only followed within the same function.

rules.description: Secret-like value in a URL query string.
rules.detection_condition: A URL literal contains a query parameter named like a secret (token, key, apikey, password, secret, auth) with a non-placeholder value.
rules.explanation: Query strings are stored in server and proxy logs and are visible in clear text over HTTP.
rules.recommendation: Send credentials in a header over TLS, and keep them out of source code.

rules.description: Interface that executes or loads code at run time.
rules.detection_condition: A call to a command execution, dynamic loading, ELF loading or embedded script interpreter API. Raised by one level in a dependency whose stated purpose is not scripting or plugin loading.
rules.explanation: Code that is loaded or interpreted at run time is not part of the reviewed firmware image; its behaviour depends on data the device receives or stores.
rules.recommendation: Confirm where the executed code comes from and that it is authenticated before it runs.
limitations: Interpreters not listed here are not recognised.

rules.description: Network-received data reaches an execution interface.
rules.detection_condition: Within one function, a value produced by a network read (Client::read, HTTPClient::getString, WebServer::arg, recv, ...) flows through variables into an EXEC001 interface or into a data-to-function-pointer cast.
rules.explanation: Executing data received from the network lets whoever controls that data run code on the device.
rules.recommendation: Do not execute received data. If remote logic is required, authenticate and sandbox it.
limitations: Data flow is tracked only inside a single function, through plain variable assignments.

rules.description: Data buffer converted to a function pointer.
rules.detection_condition: A cast whose target type is a pointer to function and whose operand is a data pointer or array.
rules.explanation: Treating data as code is how injected or downloaded machine code is run. Legitimate uses (bootloaders, JIT) are rare in application firmware.
rules.recommendation: Explain and document why data is executed; otherwise remove the cast.
limitations: Conversions through unions or memcpy are not detected.

rules.description: Firmware update capability present.
rules.detection_condition: A call to an OTA/update API (Update, HTTPUpdate, ArduinoOTA, esp_ota_*, esp_https_ota). INFO in project code; MEDIUM in a dependency whose stated purpose does not involve OTA/updates.
rules.explanation: OTA updates are a normal maintenance feature. The finding records the update path so that its authentication and transport can be reviewed.
rules.recommendation: Make sure updates are authenticated (signed images or authenticated transport).

rules.description: Network OTA enabled without a password.
rules.detection_condition: ArduinoOTA.begin() is called and no ArduinoOTA.setPassword()/setPasswordHash() call exists in the analysed code.
required_context: all ArduinoOTA calls in the project
rules.explanation: Anyone on the local network can then upload firmware to the device.
rules.recommendation: Call ArduinoOTA.setPassword() or setPasswordHash() before ArduinoOTA.begin().
limitations: A password set in code that was not parsed (parse errors, excluded files) is not seen.

rules.description: Firmware downloaded without transport security.
rules.detection_condition: HTTPUpdate::update/updateSpiffs receives a constant http:// URL, or its client object had setInsecure() called in the same function.
required_context: client configuration in the same function
rules.explanation: An attacker on the network path can replace the downloaded firmware unless images are signed and verified.
rules.recommendation: Download updates over HTTPS with certificate verification, and enable signed images.
limitations: Image signature verification (secure boot / signed OTA) is not detected and may mitigate this.

rules.description: Raw flash write or erase operation.
rules.detection_condition: A call that writes or erases flash directly (esp_flash_*, spi_flash_*, esp_partition_write/erase_range, ESP.flashWrite/flashEraseSector). Raised by one level in a dependency whose purpose does not involve storage or flash.
rules.explanation: Direct flash access can overwrite application, bootloader or configuration data if offsets are wrong or attacker-controlled.
rules.recommendation: Prefer the partition, NVS or filesystem APIs and validate offsets.

rules.description: Permanent eFuse or boot-security change.
rules.detection_condition: A call that burns eFuses or permanently enables/changes secure boot or flash encryption.
rules.explanation: eFuses are one-time programmable (datasheet section 3); a wrong value can permanently disable features or brick the device.
rules.recommendation: Keep eFuse programming in a dedicated, reviewed provisioning tool, not in application firmware.

rules.description: Boot partition changed outside a completed OTA update.
rules.detection_condition: esp_ota_set_boot_partition() is called in a function that does not also complete an OTA write (esp_ota_end / Update.end).
required_context: other calls in the same function
rules.explanation: Selecting a different boot image outside the update flow changes which firmware runs after the next reset.
rules.recommendation: Switch boot partitions only after a verified update has completed.
limitations: OTA flows split across several functions are reported.

rules.description: Debugging interface used by the firmware.
rules.detection_condition: A call that starts a debug stub or reads/erases a core dump (esp_gdbstub_init, esp_core_dump_image_get, esp_core_dump_image_erase).
rules.explanation: Debug interfaces and core dumps can expose memory contents, including secrets, in production devices.
rules.recommendation: Disable debug interfaces in production builds.
limitations: JTAG enabled by hardware/eFuse configuration is not visible in source code.

rules.description: Large encoded string literal.
rules.detection_condition: A string literal of at least 128 characters consisting of Base64 or hexadecimal characters only.
rules.explanation: Encoded blobs hide their content from code review. On their own they are common (certificates, images, test vectors).
rules.recommendation: Document what the data is, or store it in a reviewable form.
limitations: Other encodings (XOR, custom alphabets, compression) are not recognised.

rules.description: Large embedded byte array.
rules.detection_condition: An array initializer with at least 512 integer elements.
rules.explanation: Fonts, images and certificates are often embedded this way; the content cannot be reviewed as source code.
rules.recommendation: Document the origin of the data.

rules.description: Decoding and a sensitive operation occur in the same function.
rules.detection_condition: One function calls a decoding API and also a sensitive operation (code execution/loading, data-to-code cast, flash/firmware write), but no data flow between them was established.
rules.explanation: Decoding immediately before executing or writing firmware is a pattern used to hide payloads; the combination deserves review even when the data path is not visible.
rules.recommendation: Check what is decoded and where it goes.
limitations: Co-occurrence only; the decoded data may be unrelated to the sensitive operation.

rules.description: Encoded or decoded data flows into a sensitive operation.
rules.detection_condition: Within one function, data from a large encoded literal, a large embedded array or a decoding call reaches a code execution/loading call, a data-to-code cast or a flash/firmware write.
rules.explanation: Writing or executing data that was hidden in encoded form is a strong indicator that behaviour was deliberately concealed from review.
rules.recommendation: Decode the data offline and review it before trusting this code.
limitations: Data flow is tracked only inside a single function.
